title: Backpropagate through time, one step at a time
brief: Write the tanh gradient, then the gradient of one step of the cell, then the backward loop that adds each step's own loss to the carry from later steps. Every output is checked against finite differences.
hints: tanh_backward needs no z. If h = tanh(z), the slope of tanh at z is 1 - h**2, so the answer is dh * (1 - h**2).
step_backward starts with dz = tanh_backward(dh_t, h_t). Then dx_t = dz @ W_xh, dh_prev = dz @ W_hh, dW_xh = dz.T @ x_t, dW_hh = dz.T @ h_prev, and db = dz.sum(axis=0).
bptt carries a gradient from later steps. At step t, pass dH[t] + carry to step_backward, keep the dh_prev it returns as the new carry, and add its weight gradients to running totals.
The previous state at step t is h_seq[t - 1], except at t = 0, where it is h0. Using h_seq[t] there is the usual bug.
